chapter: Minton's, Louis Armstrong and the South
title: Revenge on Joe Glaser when the Modern Jazz Quartet formed
summary: Years later Glaser phoned the rehearsal wanting to manage the Quartet; Clarke hung up on him and Monte Kay managed them instead.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Yeah. Well -- oh, yeah, that's right. The Louis, and being stranded there.
Yeah.
Incidentally, that's a very wicked thing for that office to have done.
Yeah.
I mean anything could have happened.
That's right. That's right.
That's a terrible thing.
Well, a funny thing happened after that. I had some more experiences, but I was on the winning end that time.
What, later with them?
Yeah.
Well, you better tell it now. You might forget.
Well, when we formed the Modern Jazz Quartet.
Yeah. Was that Glazer?
Yeah. Well, we were rehearsing at Nola's, so the phone rings, and you know, only my closest friends

call me Klook So I went to the phone in the rehearsal. The phone rings, and there's just the four of us there rehearsing, so I went to the phone, and I said, "Hello." He said, "Is Klook there?" So I said, "Well, I don't think they're very interested, Joe." So I hung up. Just like that. So I kind of got my revenge, you know.
That's wonderful. And did it happen that way? Who did handle them?

Just great. Yeah, you never --

The background.

No. I mean, you know, he should have had enough experience to know that you never know.
That's right.
What you're doing.
